what: A record another crate lays out (hir-ty's impl table pages) could not be written or read a segment at a time with hir-def's frozen encoding: `Enc`/`Dec` are public but a segment needs their private fields (reset the per-segment macro-call tables, borrow the files and closure), and the only code doing it was private to nameres/frozen/pages.rs.
whys: pages.rs was written for one record, the def map, inside hir-def.
Its segment writer and reader are private functions over private fields of Enc and Dec.
The public surface of the encoding is one stream (Enc::finish, Dec::new_checked), which a reader decodes from its start with a closure walk and a files check a reader.
So every later record of another crate (impls, bodies, signatures) either decodes whole or copies the segment code.
Nothing said that 'a record read a part at a time' is a general need of the encoding, not of the def map.
class: A general mechanism built inside its first user, private to it.
prevention: `hir_def::nameres::frozen::segments` (Writer, files, reader) is the one home; pages.rs should use it and drop its private `write_segment`/`segment`/`closure_of`.
cause: The segment code was private to the def-map pages.
cost: a new file and a second copy of ~40 lines until pages.rs is moved onto it
